Bug_Details:
Integer literals should not start with zero since this denotes that the rest of literal will be
interpreted as an octal value.
Examples:
int i = 012;    // set i with 10 not 12
int j = 010;    // set j with 8 not 10
k = i * j;      // set k with 80 not 120
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the code by using octal values for integer literals. In Java, integer literals starting with zero are interpreted as octal values, which can lead to unexpected results.

The'showBug' method uses octal integer literals, which can lead to unexpected results. In this case, the test case expects the'showBug' method to return 120, but it actually returns 80 due to the bug.
